title: Battery storage support, parking strategy and community improvement plan
subtitle: Also: St. David Street land and Suncor agreement, speed limits, county plan response, 2024 meeting schedule, pickup trucks.
overview: Council gave municipal support resolutions to two battery energy storage proposals, one in Elora-area Aypa Power's Elora BESS and one in Belwood from Alectra Energy Solutions {{vote:m7}}. Staff had advised that such facilities belong on employment land, not prime agricultural land. The support is conditional on compliance with all municipal and provincial by-laws, policies and standards, and further planning approvals would still be required.

Council adopted an updated Community Improvement Plan covering the whole township, with incentive programs for building improvements, rental housing and larger projects {{vote:m16}}. It also approved a revised speed limit by-law with reductions including on Gerrie Road {{vote:m10}}, and an agreement with Suncor on who pays for contaminated soil during the St. David Street North reconstruction {{vote:m11}}.

After a closed session, Council authorized purchases of small corner pieces of three St. David Street North properties for traffic daylight triangles {{vote:m3}}. Council endorsed the mayor's response to the province on County Official Plan Amendment 119 {{vote:m12}}, chose option 1 for the 2024 meeting schedule {{vote:m14}}, and awarded a tender for six pickup trucks {{vote:m15}}. It also received an interim parking strategy report {{vote:m6}}, with a final report due in January 2024.

decisions.detail: Council granted municipal support resolutions for Aypa Power's Elora BESS and Alectra Energy Solutions' Belwood project, conditional on meeting all applicable municipal and provincial by-laws and standards.
Council designated the whole township as the community improvement project area and adopted the updated Community Improvement Plan by by-law.
Council authorized a new by-law to regulate speed in the township, repealing By-law 2022-52 and bringing in the speed reductions.
Council authorized an agreement with Suncor defining responsibility for excavating and disposing of contaminated soil during the St. David Street North reconstruction.

decisions.item: St. David Street North daylight triangles
decisions.detail: Council authorized agreements to buy portions of three St. David Street North properties for traffic daylight triangles at $5,000 each.
Council endorsed the head of council's response to the Minister of Municipal Affairs and Housing on reversing modifications to County OPA 119.
Council approved option 1 for the 2024 schedule, with consent agendas, and directed any needed procedure by-law amendments.
Council awarded Request for Tender #57-23 for six half-ton pickups to Finch Chevrolet Cadillac Buick GMC Ltd. at $347,734 before taxes and endorsed pre-budget funding changes.

debate: On battery storage, several councillors worried about siting the facilities on prime agricultural land, citing the township's strategic plan, staff's advice, and unanswered questions about restoring the soil after the lease term. Planning staff said such uses are generally meant for urban areas and that the planning path was uncertain.

Supporters said the resolution is an early, non-binding step. They noted the township could opt out later, planning approvals would still apply, the province treats energy supply as a priority, and the projects could bring community payments. A delegate said the support counts for a sizeable share of the provincial scoring.

A request to consider the two proposals separately was raised, citing differences in community engagement and offered benefits. Others wanted them kept together and treated equally. A councillor from the Belwood area said they had not seen notice of the delegate's community session, and the delegate described the notice steps taken.

On parking, councillors asked about a parking structure, access for emergency vehicles and downtown residents, evening parking, and staff shuttles. The consultant said a structure is on the list of options and that Fergus riverside lots could be reconfigured in the next phase.
On the community improvement plan, one councillor asked whether one developer could stack several grants. Consultant and staff said annual budgets are limited and grants are discretionary.
